A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sinkhorn-normalized diffusion framework despite the changed title and format. All 33 pages of v1 and 32 pages of v2, including appendices, support comparison of the text, equations, figures and results.

before.justification: v1 reports original spectral-analysis experiments, particle flows, shape interpolation and shape-correspondence errors, with further experimental results in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical studies and adds runtime measurements, robustness experiments, quantitative flow and deformation diagnostics, and XYZ-input correspondence results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the normalized operator, kernel formulas, Q-DiffNet architecture and losses, and normalized geodesic construction remain unchanged. The new XYZ ablation and KNN runtime configuration evaluate existing input and sparse-operator capabilities rather than revise the proposed method.

E1.justification: The principal tasks, representation families and FAUST/SCAPE/SHREC19 benchmarks are retained. v2 extends coverage within these geometric tasks through Sumner horse and cat examples, including a defective cat mesh, and Armadillo scenarios with perturbed masses and nonuniform sampling.

E2.justification: The main correspondence comparator set is unchanged. v2 adds actual runtime comparisons with CPU sparse-LU/implicit-Euler diffusion and GPU dense Cholesky and matrix-exponential implementations (Tables 1 and 3; Appendix F), which v1 discussed without reporting these timing comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 introduces substantial evaluation protocols: five-iteration timing benchmarks up to one million points, CPU KNN settings with 25 or 100 neighbors, multiplicative mass noise, nonuniform downsampling, spectral bandwidth variation, and aligned XYZ inputs. Chamfer distance and mean area distortion add quantitative evaluation metrics. Existing correspondence splits and training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test mass-estimation sensitivity (Appendix D), spectral stability under sampling and bandwidth changes (G), and dependence on WKS versus XYZ features (J). Appendices H and I quantify previously qualitative flow and deformation behavior. The earlier SHREC19 correspondence visualization in v1 Figure 6b is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The standard deviation in v2's mass-noise experiment controls the perturbation distribution; it is not uncertainty reporting for estimated performance.

E6.justification: The main correspondence scores are identical in v1 Figure 6a and v2 Table 2. Substantial new results include runtime tables, robustness curves, animal examples, Chamfer convergence and area distortion. Under the new XYZ setting, Table 4 reports SHREC19 errors of 7.68 for Q-DiffNet (Q-FM), 9.35 for DiffNet (PC), and 10.5 for ULRSSM (PC); these are additional results under different inputs, not improvements over the retained WKS scores.

T1.justification: v2 adds Proposition 4.6 and its Appendix D proof, bounding first-order relative scaling-factor error by half the relative mass perturbation and deriving the variation of Q. Appendix A also adds the converse logarithm/Metzler argument. The original normalization and refinement theorems are retained as Theorems 4.4 and 4.5.

C1.justification: The central diffusion-normalization and geometric-application claims remain. v2 omits v1's explicit novelty assertion that mass-preserving normalization had not been used on general discrete geometric structures and emphasizes fixed-scale geometry processing. Its conclusion also adds a claimed connection to reversible Markov kernels and entropy gradient flows.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive limitations concerning inaccurate mass estimates and reduced expressivity when signal amplification is useful. It explains LDDMM contraction through spectral degeneracy and interprets the XYZ ablation as evidence that engineered descriptors strongly drive benchmark performance. The absence of guaranteed convergence to a true Laplacian was already acknowledged in v1.

D1.justification: v2 newly provides a repository address for CPU/GPU implementations and documents timing scope, V100/CUDA 12.1, CPU models, PyTorch/PyKeOps and KNN configurations. v1 explicitly declined to report runtimes. Existing Q-DiffNet hyperparameters and training details are retained; mesh-derived WKS inputs were already disclosed in v1 Appendix H.

R1.justification: The main literature framework remains, but v2 refines its distinction from manifold-limit research and adds references including diffusion maps, Belkin's point-cloud Laplacian, Maas's Markov-chain gradient flows, Sumner's shapes and GreenCloud. Several earlier software and background references disappear. These are limited positioning and citation changes beyond the citation-style conversion.

P1.justification: v2 substantially rewrites prose across the introduction, related work, theoretical exposition and results. It changes the title, adds a motivation passage and a dedicated Limitations section, and reorganizes the appendices. This extends beyond wording changes required to introduce the new experiments.

P2.justification: The main text changes to two columns, Figure 1 becomes an explanatory diagram, and new tables and analytical plots are added. The correspondence results become Table 2 without the former qualitative panel. Six eigenvector plates are consolidated into three denser figures; the sphere panel remains, although v2 Figure 13 incorrectly calls it a cube.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the paper's practical claims: v1 lacked measured runtime comparisons, relied on mesh-derived descriptors in correspondence tests, and illustrated flow and deformation benefits mainly qualitatively. The new timing studies, XYZ ablation, quantitative diagnostics and proved mass-stability bound address those gaps, while explicit limitations improve interpretation. Mixed-hardware timings require care, and compressed figures introduce presentation defects, but these drawbacks are outweighed by the stronger validation and reproducibility information.
